name: AI Bug Bounty Methodology & Knowledge Base
description: Comprehensive structured methodology, checklists, and attack-vector knowledge base for the AI Bug Bounty Research Agent.

categories.name: Broken Access Control (IDOR, BOLA, Privilege Escalation)
rules: Test horizontal privilege escalation by swapping numeric, GUID, and string IDs across user accounts
Test vertical privilege escalation by invoking admin-only endpoints with lower-privileged JWT/tokens
Inspect hidden HTTP methods (GET vs POST vs PUT vs DELETE vs PATCH) on restricted endpoints
Check missing authorization in multi-step workflows (skipping payment or approval steps)

categories.name: SQL Injection
rules: Differentiate syntax errors (500) from true SQL boolean reflection or time delay
Always verify time-based SQLi with multiple delay intervals (e.g. 5s then 10s) to rule out network latency
Look for out-of-band (OAST) interactions for blind SQLi in asynchronous logging or secondary queries
Verify union-based injection column count and compatible data types before extracting data

categories.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS: Stored, Reflected, DOM)
rules: Confirm payload renders in executable browser DOM context, not solely escaped in text/HTML attributes
Verify whether modern browser defenses (HttpOnly, strict CSP, Trusted Types) mitigate practical cookie theft
For Reflected XSS, prove arbitrary victim execution via link click; verify whether anti-CSRF or POST constraints apply
For Stored XSS, confirm persistent rendering across multiple sessions and privileges

categories.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
rules: Distinguish blind DNS-only callbacks from exploitable SSRF with HTTP response body reflection
Probe cloud metadata endpoints: AWS/GCP (169.254.169.254) with required headers (X-aws-ec2-metadata-token)
Check bypasses for IP filters: 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, [::], decimal/hex IP representations, DNS rebinding
Check internal service ports (redis 6379, elasticsearch 9200, kubernetes kubelet 10250)

categories.name: Security Misconfiguration & Information Disclosure
rules: Disclose sensitive environment variables, credentials, private keys, or internal API tokens
Evaluate CORS configuration: Access-Control-Allow-Origin with wildcards or arbitrary reflected origins WITH Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Audit exposed developer endpoints: /.env, /.git/config, /actuator/env, /swagger.json, /graphql introspection
Confirm whether exposed source maps actually contain private proprietary code or hardcoded production secrets

categories.name: Identification & Authentication Failures
rules: Audit password reset flows for Host header injection, predictable tokens, or missing rate limiting
Analyze JWT tokens: algorithm confusion (RS256 to HS256), weak secret brute-force, 'none' algorithm, missing expiration
Audit OAuth 2.0 / OIDC implementations: redirect_uri validation bypasses, CSRF in state parameter, token leakage via Referer
Check session fixation and failure to invalidate tokens upon password change or logout

categories.name: Race Conditions & Business Logic Flaws
rules: Target state-sensitive operations: coupon redemption, wallet withdrawals, vote/like counters, invite code claims
Execute parallel HTTP requests using HTTP/2 single-packet multiplexing to trigger race windows
Verify negative quantities, rounding truncation, or currency confusion in payment logic
Confirm business impact: demonstrates financial loss, privilege escalation, or unauthorized asset claim
